provenance: Synthetic, hand-derived from contractual cash flows; no calculator implementation produced these expectations.

put_cases.derivation: Two contracts deliver 200 shares. Gross purchase obligation is 200 shares at 50 = 10000. Premium is 400 less one total fee of 3 = 397; 397 spread over 200 shares is 1.985; effective entry 48.015. At zero stock value, loss is 9603. Net premium divided by strike notional is 0.0397.
Thirty deliverable shares cost 375. Gross premium 22.5 less total fees 1.5 leaves 21, or 0.7 per share; effective entry is 11.8; zero-value loss is 354; 21/375 = 0.056. No USD conversion is assumed.
Ten shares earn 1 gross premium but cost 2 total fees: net -1. Negative income increases effective entry to 20.1 and zero-value loss to 201. Negative returns are preserved.

roll_cases.derivation: Original leg received 400 and costs 1000 to close: -600, or -3 per share, before fees. Replacement receives 1200. Roll cash is 1200 less 1000 less total fees 4 = 196. Combined original and roll cash is 596; the original loss remains visible. No fee allocation between legs is invented.
Original receives 37.5, closing costs 15, replacement receives 7.5. Old leg realizes 22.5; roll alone costs 9 including 1.5 total fees; combined cash is 28.5.

expiry_cases.derivation: Two short strike-50 puts owe 2000; one long strike-45 put receives 500; ten stock shares are worth 400. Net terminal value is -1100, excluding historical premiums, cost basis and fees.
Two long strike-30 calls receive 2000; one short strike-35 call owes 500; terminal payoff is 1500.
Both strike-50 and strike-45 puts have zero intrinsic value at 55. An observed zero is a known value, not a missing spot.
